comment: Liquid Dynamics dummies. Segments are capsules (a, b, radius in metres), standing with the feet at y = 0 and facing +z. A dummy is a target for spatter studies, not an injury model: it has a reservoir of liquid behind a vinyl skin and a flesh simulant the rounds cross.

dummies.name: Crash dummy
dummies.description: A generic 50th-percentile adult crash dummy (1.75 m), yellow vinyl, filled with green stage blood.

provenance.segments_m: estimated: capsules fitted to 50th-percentile adult male stature, chest breadth and depth (ANSUR II summary statistics)
provenance.tissue_density_kgm3: published: 10% ballistic gelatin and soft tissue ~1040-1060 kg/m3
provenance.tissue_strength_MPa: calibrated: Poncelet resistance R in m dv/dx = -(R A + rho Cd A v^2 / 2), set so that a 9 mm 124 gr FMJ at 360 m/s penetrates 0.65 m of 10% gelatin (FBI-protocol tests report 0.6-0.75 m)
provenance.back_spatter: estimated: back spatter is a small volume of fine drops (most under 1 mm) thrown back towards the shooter at up to ~20 m/s, as filmed by Comiskey, Yarin, Kim & Attinger (Forensic Sci. Int. 2016-2019); volume per joule, size distribution and cone are orders of magnitude, not fits
provenance.forward_spatter: estimated: forward spatter carries more liquid in larger and faster drops than back spatter (Comiskey et al. 2017-2019, Kabaliuk et al. 2014); volume per joule, size distribution and cone are orders of magnitude, not fits
provenance.bleed_ml_per_s: estimated: a slow drip from each wound after the shot, for passive drip stains
